name: Venetoclax + Dexamethasone (t(11;14) relapsed myeloma)

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Venetoclax activity in myeloma is biomarker-defined: restrict to t(11;14)-positive (or BCL2-high) relapsed/refractory disease. Use in myeloma is off-label and physician-directed. Physician decides.

supportiveCare: Infection risk is increased with venetoclax in myeloma; maintain infection surveillance and antimicrobial prophylaxis per institutional practice.
Herpes zoster (VZV) prophylaxis where a proteasome inhibitor or anti-CD38 antibody is added.
monitoring: CBC with differential and platelets before each cycle

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 to 4 neutropenia or significant infection
doseModificationRules.text: Hold venetoclax for grade 3 to 4 neutropenia or active significant infection; resume at a reduced dose per clinical review.

drugs.name: Venetoclax
drugs.notes: Venetoclax 800 mg PO once daily, taken continuously every day of the 28-day cycle, until progression or intolerance. Unlike in CLL, myeloma dosing is typically given without a formal weekly ramp-up, but the treating team may still initiate cautiously per BCL2-inhibitor safety practice. Restrict to t(11;14)-positive disease. Own wording from standard-of-care knowledge; physician decides.

provenance.locator: t(11;14) relapsed myeloma, venetoclax + dexamethasone regimen

drugs.name: Dexamethasone
drugs.notes: Dexamethasone 40 mg PO weekly on days 1, 8, 15, and 22 of each 28-day cycle. Reduce to 20 mg weekly for patients over 75 years or frail. Own wording from standard-of-care knowledge; physician decides.

provenance.locator: weekly dexamethasone partner in relapsed-myeloma doublets
